hot.title: OPRD: On-Policy Representation Distillation
hot.summary: OPRD introduces on-policy representation distillation, a method to align student large language model (LLM) hidden states directly with a teacher model during self-play. This approach effectively closes the performance gap between student and teacher on mathematical reasoning benchmarks by up to 2.7 points over existing methods, while reducing training time by 1.44x and transient GPU memory by up to 54%.

hot.title: Agents' Last Exam
hot.summary: The University of California, Berkeley and collaborators introduce Agents’ Last Exam (ALE), a benchmark that evaluates AI agents on economically valuable, long-horizon professional tasks using real software and verifiable outputs. Frontier AI agents currently achieve low pass rates, with the top configuration reaching 26.2% overall and under 10% on the hardest tier, revealing substantial room for improvement in real-world capabilities.

hot.title: MAI-Thinking-1: Building a Hill-Climbing Machine
hot.summary: Microsoft AI developed MAI-Thinking-1, a 35B active / 1T total parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, using a "hill-climbing machine" framework for continuous, systematic improvement by training exclusively on human-generated data. The model achieved competitive performance against other frontier LLMs in STEM reasoning, coding, and general capabilities, while maintaining a strong helpfulness-safety balance.

hot.title: Latent Reasoning with Normalizing Flows
hot.summary: NF-CoT integrates autoregressive normalizing flows into large language models to enable continuous latent reasoning, replacing verbose textual Chain-of-Thought with compact thought vectors while preserving key LLM properties. This framework achieves an average 13.0% improvement in pass@1 on Python code generation benchmarks over the Qwen3-8B-Base model and is 1.92 times faster overall than diffusion-based latent reasoning methods.

hot.title: World-Language-Action Model for Unified World Modeling, Language Reasoning, and Action Synthesis
hot.summary: The World-Language-Action (WLA) model introduces a unified embodied foundation model that integrates world modeling, language reasoning, and action synthesis using an autoregressive Transformer backbone. It demonstrated superior performance on complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks in simulations and real-world scenarios, while achieving significantly reduced inference latency and the ability to learn novel tasks from action-free videos.

hot.title: OrderGrad: Optimizing Beyond the Mean with Order-Statistic Policy Gradient Estimation
hot.summary: OrderGrad introduces a unified framework for optimizing arbitrary finite-sample L-statistic objectives in stochastic learning, providing unbiased likelihood-ratio and reparameterization gradient estimators. It improves performance in LLM math reasoning tasks, enables effective multi-objective optimization, and offers precise control over gradient pressure across reward distributions.

hot.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
hot.summary: Researchers from Shanghai AI Laboratory and East China Normal University developed MLEvolve, a self-evolving multi-agent framework for automated, end-to-end machine learning algorithm discovery. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MLE-Bench benchmark and demonstrates robust generalization across various optimization tasks by integrating progressive search, retrospective memory, and hierarchical planning.

hot.title: Pretraining Recurrent Networks without Recurrence
hot.summary: Supervised Memory Training (SMT) enables the time-parallel training of nonlinear Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) by framing memory transitions as a supervised learning problem, where a Transformer "teacher" provides optimal memory states. This method overcomes the limitations of traditional Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT), allowing RNNs to effectively learn long-range dependencies and achieve strong performance on diverse sequence modeling tasks with fixed-memory inference.

hot.title: OneReason Technical Report
hot.summary: OneReason is a generative recommendation foundation model that integrates robust itemic token perception and sophisticated, recommendation-specific cognition. It enables a "thinking mode" to consistently outperform a "non-thinking mode" on Kuaishou's real-world benchmarks, resulting in significant online business uplifts.

hot.title: On Advantage Estimates for Max@K Policy Gradients
hot.summary: Researchers at The University of Tokyo developed MaxPO, an optimization method for max@K policy gradients that introduces a Leave-Two-Out (L2O) baseline to center the advantage estimate. This approach reduced gradient variance by 77.4% on average and improved pass@256 performance by up to 5.2% on math reasoning benchmarks for large language models.

hot.title: dots.tts Technical Report
hot.summary: The "dots.tts" system, developed by researchers at dots, Xiaohongshu Inc. and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, introduces a 2B-parameter continuous autoregressive text-to-speech foundation model designed to overcome long-range error accumulation in continuous latent generation. It achieves high fidelity and robust zero-shot voice cloning, outperforming baselines in speaker similarity and text faithfulness while enabling efficient real-time inference.

hot.title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
hot.summary: NVIDIA introduces Cosmos 3, a family of omnimodal world models that jointly process and generate language, image, video, audio, and action sequences within a unified Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for Physical AI. This framework achieves competitive to state-of-the-art performance across 48 understanding benchmarks and leads open-source models in various image, video, and robot policy generation tasks, including a 39.7% success rate on RoboLab.

hot.title: Flash-WAM: Modality-Aware Distillation for World Action Models
hot.summary: Researchers at Northeastern University and the University of Georgia developed Flash-WAM, a modality-aware distillation framework that accelerates World-Action Models (WAMs) for robotics, achieving a 23x speedup and reducing inference latency to 348 ms per control chunk, enabling real-time closed-loop robot operation while largely preserving task success rates.

hot.title: Code2LoRA: Hypernetwork-Generated Adapters for Code Language Models under Software Evolution
hot.summary: A hypernetwork-based framework, Code2LoRA, generates repository-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters for code language models, effectively injecting repository knowledge parametrically without inference-time token overhead. Its evolutionary variant adapts to changing codebases by processing sequential diffs, achieving up to a 9.9 percentage point Exact Match improvement over strong baselines in repository-level assertion completion tasks.

hot.title: LARA: Latent Action Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
hot.summary: The LARA (Latent Action Representation Alignment) framework jointly optimizes Latent Action Models (LAMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by explicitly aligning their intermediate latent representations. This approach enhances VLA model performance and generalization capabilities across various robotic manipulation benchmarks, achieving improved success rates and better adaptation to novel tasks and embodiments.

hot.title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
hot.summary: AffordanceVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model developed by researchers at Peking University and collaborators, utilizes structured affordance forecasting as an intermediate representation to improve robotic manipulation. This system achieved an average success rate of 95.8% on the LIBERO benchmark and an Average Length of 4.33 on CALVIN, while also demonstrating enhanced instruction-following and emergent long-horizon capabilities in real-world scenarios.

hot.title: MMAE: A Massive Multitask Audio Editing Benchmark
hot.summary: A new benchmark, MMAE (Massive Multitask Audio Editing), provides a comprehensive, rubric-based evaluation for instruction-guided audio editing systems across diverse modalities and complexities. Evaluations on leading models demonstrate that current systems achieve Exact Match Rates below 5%, revealing significant limitations in handling complex, mixed-modality tasks and balancing instruction following with audio consistency.

hot.title: Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments
hot.summary: Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and Snorkel AI introduced CL-BENCH, a benchmark designed to evaluate how AI systems learn and improve in real-world, stateful environments with concept drift. Their evaluation of frontier models revealed that full-context In-Context Learning (ICL) achieved the highest aggregate normalized reward and gain (22.3% and 25.4% respectively), often outperforming more complex, dedicated memory architectures.

hot.title: Thinking with Imagination: Agentic Visual Spatial Reasoning with World Simulators
hot.summary: A framework called Astra allows Vision-Language Models to perform agentic visual spatial reasoning by actively acquiring imagined visual evidence from a spatially consistent world simulator. This approach improves spatial reasoning performance for a Qwen3-VL-8B backbone by up to 9.0 absolute points on MMSI-Bench and 5.9 on MindCube.

hot.title: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective
hot.summary: This paper examines why Muon outperforms Adam in Large Language Model training, identifying that its efficiency arises from encountering a lower Normalized Directional Sharpness (NDS) and thus a smaller second-order curvature penalty. It empirically demonstrates Muon's ability to achieve a larger one-step loss decrease due to this curvature property and supports these findings with a theoretical analysis using stylized quadratic models.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile Edge Computing
likes.summary: Researchers developed a multi-tier task offloading framework for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing, incorporating sequential subtask dependencies and multi-access resource allocation. This approach achieved at least a 15% reduction in average energy consumption for intelligent vehicular applications compared to existing benchmark methods.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
